Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.hebrew: עד שיכלו וכו' - אוצר יש ושמו גוף, ומבראשית נוצרו כל הנשמות העתידות להולד, ונתנם לשם:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.english: Until they are finished, etc. - There is a treasury whose name is Guf, and from the beginning [of Creation], all the souls destined to be born were created, and He placed them there.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.hebrew: כי לא לעולם אריב - לאחר זמן הגאולה, ולא לנצח אקצוף — מלגאול. כי רוח אשר לפני — נשמות שבגוף; יעטוף — הוא המאחר, כמו העטופים ללבן (בראשית ל׳:מ״ב), ונשמות שאני עשיתי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.english: For I will not contend forever - [That is, not] beyond the time of the redemption; and "neither will I be always wroth" — [refraining] from redeeming [them]. For "the spirit that is before Me" [refers to] the souls in the Guf; "shall delay" — this means delaying, like "the late-born were Laban's" (Genesis 30:42); and "the souls that I have made."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:11:1.hebrew: כמי שלא באנו לעולם - לפי שהן חיים לעולם, וכל זמן שהן קיימין, אין אנו חשובין כלום:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:11:1.english: As though we had not come into the world - Because they would live forever, and as long as they exist, we are considered nothing.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:14:1.hebrew: הא לא קבלו ישראל את התורה - הוי שומע מכאן, שלא קבלוה לקבל שכר היום בעולם הזה, אלא שלא תהא אומה ולשון שולטת בהן, וזו היא טובה הכתובה כאן: למען ייטב להם:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:14:1.english: Behold, Israel did not accept the Torah [except] - Infer from here that they did not accept it to receive reward today, in this world, but rather so that no nation or tongue would rule over them, and this is the goodness written here: "That it might be good for them."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:17:1.hebrew: עניות - שמשחטאו, שלטו בהן שונאיהם, המכלים את ממונם כל היום, בוהיה לאכול:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:17:1.english: Poverty - For once they sinned, their enemies ruled over them, who consume their wealth all day, with which there was [food] to eat.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:18:1.hebrew: דתן ואבירם - דאמר מר (נדרים דף סד:): כל מקום שנאמר נצים, נצבים, אינן אלא דתן ואבירם. והכא במבקשי נפשו כתי' נצים, היינו אותן עברים שהלשינו עליו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:18:1.english: Dathan and Abiram - For the Master said (Nedarim 64b): Wherever it is stated "quarreling" [or] "standing," they are none other than Dathan and Abiram. And here, regarding those who sought his life, it is written "quarreling" — that is, those Hebrews who informed on him.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:1:1.english: To say to you - It was a decree of the King to give an opening of the mouth [to plead] to penitents.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:20:1.hebrew: וכן הוא אומר לו עמי שומע לי - שהקב"ה מתחנן לפניהם שישמרו את התורה. לו עמי היינו תחינה, כמו הן לו יהי כדברך (בראשית ל׳:ל״ד):
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:20:1.english: And similarly, it states: "Would that My people would listen to Me" - For the Holy One, Blessed be He, pleads with them to observe the Torah. "Would that My people" is [an expression of] supplication, like: "Behold, would that it be according to your word" (Genesis 30:34).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:21:1.english: Ingrates - They do not recognize [the obligation] to show gratitude to [their] benefactor.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:2:1.hebrew: דמפרסם חטאיהן - ואיכא חילול, אימא לא ליתקבלו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:2:1.english: Whose sin is publicized - And there is a desecration [of God's Name], [so one might] say that they should not be accepted [in repentance].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:4:1.hebrew: מלפפתו - מעטפתו, לשון מלבוש, כמו מלפפין את התינוק בשבת (שבת דף קכט:):
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:4:1.english: Enwraps him - Cloaks him, an expression of clothing, as in: "One swaddles an infant on Shabbat" (Shabbat 129b).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.english: To our ancestors - Those who made the [Golden] Calf.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:2.english: We would not have come into the world - For they would have been like angels and would not have begotten children.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:7:1.hebrew: לשמחת עונה - שעד עתה נאסר להן, אל תגשו אל אשה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:7:1.english: For the joy of marital relations - For until now, it was forbidden to them: "Do not approach a woman."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:8:1.english: To those - Children who were already [alive] at their standing at Sinai.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.hebrew: אין בן דוד בא עד שיכלו נשמות שבגוף - וא"ת: מ"מ יכלו ע"י עובדי כוכבים שיהו מולידים? ואומר הר"ר אלחנן, דנשמות של ישראל ושל עובדי כוכבים אינן בגוף א'. והא דאמר (שבת ל:) עתידה אשה שתלד בכל יום לימות המשיח, שמא י"ל: גוף חדש ונשמות חדשות יהיו:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.english: The son of David does not come until the souls in the Guf are exhausted - And if you say: Nevertheless, let [the souls] be exhausted through idolaters, who give birth? And Rabbeinu Elchanan says that the souls of Israel and of idolaters are not in one [and the same] Guf. And as for that which [the Gemara] says (Shabbat 30b): "In the future, a woman will give birth every day" in the days of the Messiah — perhaps one can say: There will be a new Guf and new souls.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.hebrew: כי רוח מלפני יעטוף - משיח נקרא רוח, כדכתיב (איכה ד׳:כ׳) רוח אפינו משיח ה'. וה"פ דקרא: המשיח מלפני יאחר, כמו העטופים ללבן, על ידי נשמות אשר עשיתי:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.english: For the spirit from before Me shall enwrap - The Messiah is called "spirit," as it is written (Lamentations 4:20): "The breath [ru'ach] of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord." And this is the explanation of the verse: The Messiah will be delayed from [coming before] Me, like "the late-born were Laban's" (Genesis 30:42), on account of the souls that I have made.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:18:1.hebrew: אלא שירדו מנכסיהם - דליכא למימר סומים היו, דהא כתיב בעדת קרח (במדבר ט״ז:י״ד) העיני האנשים ההם תנקר; ומצורעים נמי לא הוו, דהא בעדה בתוך המחנה היו יושבין. וכ"ת דבמתן תורה נתרפאו — דהא אותן שנתרפאו כבר חזרו למומן במעשה העגל. ושלא היו להם בנים ליכא למימר, דבשביל כך לא היו פחות קרובים למלכות להלשינו כבתחלה. וי"מ דמשמע ליה שירדו מנכסיהם, דמחמת כן אין להן כח עוד להזיק; אבל כל הנך היו יכולין להזיקו ע"י ממונם. ופשטיה דקרא מיירי בפרעה, וימת מלך מצרים:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:18:1.english: Rather, that they lost their property - For one cannot say [that] they were blind, as behold, it is written regarding the assembly of Korah (Numbers 16:14): "Will you gouge out the eyes of those men?" And they were also not lepers, for behold, they were dwelling in the assembly within the camp. And if you were to say that at the Giving of the Torah they were healed — behold, those who were healed already returned to their blemish during the incident of the [Golden] Calf. And one cannot say that they had no children, for on account of that they would not have been any less close to the royal court to slander him as [they did] initially. And some explain that [the Gemara] understood that they lost their property because on account of that they no longer had power to cause harm, whereas [in] all of those [other cases] they would have been able to harm him by means of their money. And the plain meaning of the verse refers to Pharaoh: "And the king of Egypt died" [Exodus 2:23].

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:21:1.hebrew: כפויי טובה - לכך קראם כפויי טובה, שלא רצו לומר אתה תן, לפי שלא היו רוצים להחזיק לו טובה בכך:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:21:1.english: Ingrates - For this reason [Moses] called them ingrates: because they did not want to say, "You give [it]," since they did not want to be grateful to Him for that.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:2:1.english: And it is necessary - That is, [it was necessary] to record their sin and the acceptance of their repentance.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.hebrew: שאלמלא לא חטאו לא באנו לעולם - ואע"ג דאמרינן פ"ק דערובין (דף יג: ושם): נמנו וגמרו נוח לו לאדם שלא נברא, היינו בתחלת לידתו, שאין ידוע מה יהא בסופו; אבל כשהוא צדיק, אשריו ואשרי הדור שהוא בתוכו. ועוד, דלמסקנא דכמי שלא באנו לעולם, אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.english: For had they not sinned, we would not have come into the world - And even though we say in the first chapter of Eruvin (13b, and there): "They counted and concluded: It would have been better for man not to have been created" — that is at the beginning of his birth, when it is not known what his end will be; but when he is righteous, happy is he and happy is the generation in whose midst he is. And furthermore, according to the conclusion [of the Gemara] that [it means] "as though we had not come into the world," it works out well.
